name: Readiness
question: Which targets can this dataset serve, decided before generating?
purpose: Turn the known limits into a prediction made in advance rather than an excuse afterwards.
verdict_rule: the worst grade of its graded metrics
caveats: Training support at a target is only a PROXY for label error, and it did not transfer. It was calibrated on Perov-5, where 96% of gaps are exactly zero so the non-zero region really is sparse. On the user's 246-structure upload, whose gaps are continuous over 0.6-14 eV, every target fails the support count while the measured held-out error is 0.179 spreads, and support barely correlates with error (Spearman -0.11). So when a model exists, `holdout_label_error` supersedes the count; the count is kept for the preview, where no model has been trained yet.

metrics.name: Targets with enough support
metrics.definition: Number of requested targets whose training support passes the S0 support band.
metrics.meaning_good: At least one requested target is supported by the data.
metrics.remedy: Choose targets inside the supported range.
metrics.reference_note: Perov-5: 0 to 3.5 eV servable; 4 eV and above unreliable (22, 14, 8 and 7 materials). Validated against the outcome: targets called servable gave a mean label error of 0.59 eV, those called unreliable 0.95 eV.

metrics.name: Measured label error on the held-out split
metrics.definition: Mean absolute error of the target on the held-out test split, divided by the spread of that split.
metrics.meaning_good: Labels on unseen materials are accurate, measured rather than predicted.
metrics.meaning_bad: Labels on unseen materials are not accurate enough to aim a target at.
metrics.remedy: More data, or restrict targets to the range the model demonstrably handles.
metrics.reference_note: On the user's 246-structure upload this is 0.179 spreads (0.647 eV on a 3.62 eV spread) even though every target fails the support count, which is why the count is only a proxy.

metrics.name: Is latent distance usable as an uncertainty signal
metrics.definition: Correlation between a material's latent distance to the training set and its prediction error.
metrics.meaning_good: Latent distance can be used to flag untrustworthy candidates.
metrics.meaning_bad: Latent distance carries no information on this dataset and must not be quoted as uncertainty.
metrics.remedy: Fall back to training support at the target, which does work.
metrics.reference_note: -0.12 on Perov-5: a complete grid leaves the axis no range, since every test material almost touches a training one. The block reports the axis as unusable instead of quoting a meaningless number. It is re-tested per dataset, never assumed.
